title: Homes as Assets
sentences: A house performs two functions that turn out to be quietly incompatible with each other.
It shelters a household, and it stores a large share of that household's accumulated wealth.
For several decades those two functions could be pursued without any visible conflict.
Sustained price growth eventually made the second of them the dominant consideration.
A society that needs housing to be cheap cannot simultaneously need it to appreciate.
Most political argument about housing carefully avoids stating that tension plainly.
Existing owners are numerous, well organised and entirely understandably protective.
Those who need to buy are younger, more dispersed and rarely decisive at elections.
The outcome follows from that arithmetic rather than from anybody's particular conspiracy.
Very little of it resolves until one of the two functions is openly given clear priority.
